cands.name: David L. Faulkner

money.note: Covers January 2023 on, primary and general. Party-committee lines are often in-kind staff and mail.
money.source: Alabama Fair Campaign Practices Act system, downloaded Nov 5, 2026

cands.bio: Republican state representative for Alabama House District 46 (parts of Mountain Brook, Homewood and Hoover) since 2014. A civil trial attorney with Christian & Small in Birmingham. Graduate of the University of Alabama and its School of Law. Vice Chair of the House Rules Committee.

endorsements.text: In 2014 his endorsers included the Alabama Farmers' Federation and the Alabama Trucking Association. Ballotpedia found no endorsements for the 2026 race.

cands.gaps: We could not find his birthplace, where he grew up, or when he came to Alabama. We found no documented votes, bills or public statements from him on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buying, growth and land conservation, immigration or H-1B, police pay and pensions, gun laws, abortion, or vouchers and charters. His campaign site describes education bills (computer science, a camp safety act) and a teacher pay raise in the education budget, but the pages we could read did not show his own vote on the raise. The campaign news items were only short summaries, and the Ballotpedia list of bills he sponsored did not load. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in 2022 or 2026. We found no controversies, foreign ties or 2026 endorsements.

qual.background: Alabama House member since November 2014 (about 12 years), and a civil litigation and business trial attorney with a University of Alabama law degree.
qual.why: Long prior legislative service combined with a law career fits the top band for writing law and budgets. His committee posts, including Vice Chair of Rules, were not counted.
